26 to all.

As a woman working in the first half of the 20th century, Franklin's contributions to some of the greatest scientific discoveries of our time including the structure of DNA-were sadly 27 in her ----lifetime.

More than 60 years after Franklin's death, we are ----28 living in a different world, where women play an important part in every echelon (阶层) of our society-not least in science, innovation, higher education and research. UK universities are world leaders when it comes to advancing and
29 gender equality.

In the past decade, we have seen a 30 increase in England in the number of women accepted ----on to full-time undergraduate degrees in science, technology, engineering and maths (Stem subjects) . And in the last academic year, women 31 for more than half of all Stem postgraduates at UK universities

Data shows us the 32 to success gets harder for women to climb the further up they go. Although women make up the majority of undergraduates in our universities, just under half of academic staff are female. Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: How to Eat Well
paragraphs.translationZh: 如何吃得好

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Why do so many Americans eat tons of processed food, the stuff that is correctly called junk (垃圾) and should really carry warning labels?
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 为什么这么多美国人吃大量的加工食品，这些食品被正确地称为垃圾，应该贴上警告标签？

paragraphs.sourceText: B) It's not because fresh ingredients are hard to come by. Supermarkets offer more variety than ever, and there are over four times as many farmers' markets in the US as there were 20 years ago. Nor is it for lack of available information. There are plenty of recipes (食谱), how-to videos and cooking classes available to anyone who has a computer, smartphone or television. If anything, the information is overwhelming.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 这并不是因为新鲜食材很难获得。超市提供的商品种类比以往任何时候都多，美国的农贸市场数量是 20 年前的四倍多。也不是因为缺乏可用信息。拥有电脑、智能手机或电视的任何人都可以使用大量食谱 (食谱)、操作视频和烹饪课程。如果有的话，信息是压倒性的。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) And yet we aren't cooking. If you eat three meals a day and behave like most Americans, you probably get at least a third of your daily calories ��������� outside the home. Nearly two-thirds of us grab fast food once a week, and we get almost 25% of our daily calories from snacks. So we're eating out or taking in, and we don't sit down-or we do, but we hurry.
D) Shouldn't preparing-and consuming-food be a source of comfort, pride, health, well-being, relaxation, task, especially when outsourcing it is so harmful?

E) When I talk about cooking, I'm not talking about creating elaborate dinner parties or three-day science projects. I'm talking about simple, easy, everyday meals. My mission is to encourage green hands and those lacking time or money to feed themselves. That means we need modest, realistic expectations, and we need to teach people to cook food that's good enough to share with family and friends.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 当我谈论烹饪时，我并不是在谈论精心策划的晚宴或为期三天的科学项目。我说的是简单、容易的日常饮食。我的使命是鼓励新手和那些缺乏时间或金钱养活自己的人。这意味着我们需要适度、现实的期望，我们需要教人们烹饪出足以与家人和朋友分享的美味食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Perhaps a return to real cooking needn't be far off. A recent Harris poll revealed that 79% of Americans say they enjoy cooking and 30% "love it"; 14% admit to not enjoying kitchen work and just 7% won't go near the stove at all. But this doesn't necessarily translate to real cooking, and the result of this survey shouldn't surprise anyone: 52% of those 65 or older cook at home five or more times per week; only a third of young people do.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 也许回归真正的烹饪并不遥远。最近的哈里斯民意调查显示，79% 的美国人表示他们喜欢烹饪，30% 的人“喜欢它”； 14% 的人承认不喜欢厨房工作，只有 7% 的人根本不会靠近炉子。但这并不一定意味着真正的烹饪，这项调查的结果不应让任何人感到惊讶：65 岁或以上的老年人中，有 52% 每周在家做饭五次或以上；只有三分之一的年轻人这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Back in the 1950s most of us grew up in households where Mom cooked virtually every night. The intention to put a home-cooked meal on the table was pretty much universal. Most people couldn't afford to do otherwise.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 早在 20 世纪 50 年代，我们大多数人都是在妈妈几乎每晚做饭的家庭中长大的。把一顿家常饭菜摆上餐桌的愿望几乎是普遍的。大多数人没有能力采取其他措施。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Although frozen dinners were invented in the '40s, their popularity didn't boom until televisions became popular a decade or so later. Since then, packaged, pre-prepared meals have been what's for dinner. The microwave and fast-food chains were the biggest catalysts ������������ , but the big food companies-which want to sell anything except the raw ingredients that go into cooking-made the home cook an endangered species.

I) Still, I find it strange that only a third of young people report preparing meals at home regularly. Isn't this the same crowd that rails against processed junk and champions craft cooking? And isn't this the generation who say they're concerned about their health and the well-being of the planet? If these are truly the values of many young people, then their behavior doesn't match their beliefs.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 不过，我觉得很奇怪的是，只有三分之一的年轻人表示定期在家做饭。这不就是反对加工垃圾和拥护手工烹饪的同一群人吗？难道这代人不是说他们关心自己的健康和地球的福祉吗？如果这些确实是许多年轻人的价值观，那么他们的行为就与他们的信仰不符。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) There have been half-hearted but well-publicized efforts by some food companies to reduce calories in their processed foods, but the Standard American Diet is still the polar opposite of the healthy, mostly plant­ based diet that just about every expert says we should be eating. Considering that the government's standards are not nearly ambitious enough, the picture is clear: by not cooking at home, we're not eating the right things, and the consequences are hard to overstate.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 一些食品公司为减少加工食品中的卡路里做出了半心半意但广为人知的努力，但标准美国饮食仍然与健康的、以植物为主的饮食截然相反，几乎每个专家都认为我们应该吃这种饮食。考虑到政府的标准还不够雄心勃勃，情况就很清楚了：如果不在家做饭，我们就吃不到正确的东西，其后果怎么强调都不为过。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) To help quantify ( i 1t) the costs of a poor diet, I recently tried to estimate this impact in terms of a most the damage they cause in health problems and environmental harm.
L) Cooking real food is the best defense-not to mention that any meal you're likely to eat at home contains about 200 fewer calories than one you would eat in a restaurant.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 烹饪真正的食物是最好的防御——更不用说您在家吃的任何一顿饭都比在餐馆吃的饭菜少大约 200 卡路里。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) To those Americans for whom money is a concern, my advice is simple: Buy what you can afford, and cook it yourself. The common prescription is to primarily shop the grocery store, since that's where fresh produce, meat and seafood, and dairy are. And to save money and still eat well you don't need local, organic ingredients; all you need is real food. I'm not saying local food isn't better; it is. But there is plenty of decent food in the grocery stores.
paragraphs.translationZh: M）对于那些关心钱的美国人，我的建议很简单：买你能买得起的东西，然后自己做饭。常见的做法是主要去杂货店购买，因为那里有新鲜农产品、肉类、海鲜和乳制品。为了省钱又吃得好，你不需要当地的有机原料；你所需要的只是真正的食物。我并不是说当地的食物不好；而是说当地的食物不好。这是。但杂货店里有很多像样的食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) The other sections you should get to know are the frozen foods and the canned goods. Frozen produce is still produce; canned tomatoes are still tomatoes. Just make sure you're getting real food without tons of added salt or sugar. Ask yourself, would Grandma consider this food? Does it look like something that might occur in nature? It's pretty much common sense: you want to buy food, not unidentifiable foodlike objects.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 您应该了解的其他部分是冷冻食品和罐头食品。冷冻产品仍然是产品；罐装西红柿仍然是西红柿。只要确保您吃的是真正的食物，不添加大量的盐或糖即可。问问你自己，奶奶会考虑这个食物吗？它看起来像自然界中可能发生的事情吗？这几乎是常识：你想买食物，而不是无法识别的类似食物的物品。

paragraphs.sourceText: 0) You don't have to hit the grocery store daily, nor do you need an abundance of skill. Since fewer than half of Americans say they cook at an intermediate level and only 20% describe their cooking skills as advanced, the crisis is one of confidence. And the only remedy for that is practice. There's nothing mysterious about cooking the evening meal. You just have to do a little thinking ahead and redefine what qualifies as dinner. Like any skill, cooking gets easier as you do it more; every time you cook, you advance your level of skills. Someday you won't even need recipes. My advice is that you not pay attention to the number of steps and ingredients, because they can be deceiving. P) Time, I realize, is the biggest obstacle to cooking for most people. You must adjust your priorities to find time to cook. For instance, you can move a TV to the kitchen and watch your favorite shows while you're standing at the sink. No one is asking you to give up activities you like, but if you're watching food shows on TV, try cooking instead.
paragraphs.translationZh: 0) 你不必每天都去杂货店，也不需要丰富的技能。由于只有不到一半的美国人表示自己的烹饪水平处于中级水平，只有 20% 的人称自己的烹饪技能较高，因此这场危机是一场信心危机。唯一的补救办法就是练习。做饭并没有什么神秘的。你只需要提前思考一下，重新定义什么才算是晚餐。就像任何技能一样，烹饪越多就会变得越容易。每次你做饭，你的技能水平都会提高。有一天你甚至不需要食谱。我的建议是你不要注意步骤和成分的数量，因为它们可能是骗人的。 P) 我意识到，对于大多数人来说，时间是做饭的最大障碍。你必须调整你的优先顺序才能找到做饭的时间。例如，您可以将电视移至厨房，然后站在水槽旁观看您喜爱的节目。没有人要求您放弃您喜欢的活动，但如果您正在电视上观看美食节目，请尝试做饭。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Cooking benefits people in many ways and enables them to connect with one another.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 烹饪在很多方面使人们受益，并使他们能够相互联系。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Abundant information about cooking is available either online or on TV.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 网上或电视上提供了大量有关烹饪的信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Young people do less cooking at home than the elderly these days.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 如今，年轻人在家做饭的次数比老年人少。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Cooking skills can be improved with practice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 烹饪技巧可以通过练习来提高。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. In the mid-20th century, most families ate dinner at home instead of eating out.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 20世纪中叶，大多数家庭在家吃晚饭，而不是外出就餐。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Even those short of time or money should be encouraged to cook for themselves and their family.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 即使那些缺乏时间或金钱的人也应该被鼓励为自己和家人做饭。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Eating food not cooked by ourselves can cause serious consequences.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42、吃自己没有煮过的食物会造成严重的后果。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. To eat well and still save money, people should buy fresh food and cook it themselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 为了吃得好又省钱，人们应该购买新鲜食物并自己做饭。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. We get a fairly large portion of calories from fast food and snacks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44.我们从快餐和零食中获取相当大部分的卡路里。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. The popularity of TV led to the popularity of frozen food.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45.电视的普及导致了冷冻食品的流行。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The wallet is heading for extinction. As a day-to-day essential, it will die off with the generation who read print newspapers. The kind of shopping-where you hand over notes and count out change in return-now happens only in the most minor of our retail encounters, like buying a bar of chocolate or a pint of milk, from a corner shop. At the shops where you spend any real money, that money is increasingly abstracted. And this is more and more true, the higher up the scale you go. At the most cutting-edge retail stores-Victoria Beckham on Dover Street, for instance-you don't go and stand at any kind of cash register, when you decide to pay. The staff are equipped with iPads to take your payment while you relax on a sofa.
paragraphs.translationZh: 钱包正走向消亡。作为日常必需品，它将随着阅读纸质报纸的一代人而消失。这种购物方式——交出纸币并清点零钱——现在只发生在我们最微小的零售遭遇中，比如从街角商店购买一块巧克力或一品脱牛奶。在你花任何真钱的商店里，这些钱越来越抽象。级别越高，这一点就越正确。在最前沿的零售商店——例如多佛街的维多利亚·贝克汉姆——当你决定付款时，你不会走到任何收银台前。当您在沙发上休息时，工作人员会配备 iPad 来收取您的付款。

paragraphs.sourceText: Which is nothing more or less than excellent service, if you have the money. But across society, the abstraction of the idea of cash makes me uneasy. Maybe I'm just old-fashioned. But earning money isn't quick or easy for most of us. Isn't it a bit weird that spending it should happen in half a blink (眨眼) of an eye? Doesn't a wallet-that time-honoured Friday-night feeling of pleasing, promising fatness-represent something that matters?
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你有钱的话，这无非就是优质的服务。但在整个社会，现金概念的抽象让我感到不安。也许我只是守旧。但对于我们大多数人来说，赚钱并不快速或容易。眨眼间就花完了，这不是有点奇怪吗？钱包——周五晚上那种令人愉悦、有希望的肥胖的感觉——难道不代表着某种重要的东西吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: But I'll leave the economics to the experts. What bothers me about the death of the wallet is the change it represents in our physical environment. Everything about the look and feel of a wallet-the way the fastenings and materials wear and tear and loosen with age, the plastic and paper and gold and silver, and handwritten phone numbers and printed cinema tickets-is the very opposite of what our world is becoming. The opposite of a wallet is a smartphone or an iPad. The rounded edges, cool glass, smooth and unknowable as a pebble ����������� . Instead of digging through pieces of paper and peering into corners, we move our fingers left and right. No more counting out coins. Show your wallet, if you still have one. It may not be here much longer.
46. What is happening to the wallet?
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 钱包发生了什么变化？

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. How are business transactions done in big modern stores?
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 现代大型商店中的商业交易是如何进行的？

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. What makes the author feel uncomfortable nowadays?
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 是什么让作者现在感到不舒服？

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Why does the author choose to write about what's happening to the wallet?
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 为什么作者选择写钱包发生的事情？

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. What can we infer from the passage about the author?
paragraphs.translationZh: 50.从有关作者的段落中我们可以推断出什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: It's late in the evening: time to close the book and turn off the computer. You're done for the day. What you may not realize, however, is that the learning process actually continues-in your dreams.
paragraphs.translationZh: 夜已深了：该合上书本，关掉电脑了。你这一天的工作就结束了。然而，您可能没有意识到，学习过程实际上仍在继续——在您的梦中。

paragraphs.sourceText: It might sound like science fiction, but researchers are increasingly focusing on the relationship between the knowledge and skills our brains absorb during the day and the fragmented, often bizarre imaginings they generate at night. Scientists have found that dreaming about a task we've learned is associated with improved performance in that activity (suggesting that there's some truth to the popular notion that we're "getting" a foreign language once we begin dreaming in it) . What's more, researchers are coming to recognize that dreaming is an essential part of understanding, organizing and retaining what we learn.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这听起来可能像科幻小说，但研究人员越来越关注我们的大脑在白天吸收的知识和技能与它们在晚上产生的支离破碎、常常是怪异的想象之间的关系。科学家们发现，梦见我们学到的一项任务与该活动中表现的提高有关（这表明，一旦我们开始做梦，我们就“掌握”了一门外语，这一流行观点是有一定道理的）。更重要的是，研究人员逐渐认识到，做梦是理解、组织和保留所学知识的重要组成部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: While we sleep, research indicates, the brain replays the patterns of activity it experienced during
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究表明，当我们睡觉时，大脑会重播睡眠期间经历的活动模式。

paragraphs.sourceText: example of such replay can be seen in a video researchers made recently about sleep disorders. They taught a series of dance moves to a group of patients with conditions like sleepwalking, in which the sleeper engages in the kind physical movement that does not normally occur during sleep. They then videotaped the subjects as they slept. Lying in bed, eyes closed, one female patient on the tape performs the dance moves she learned earlier.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员最近制作的有关睡眠障碍的视频中可以看到这种重播的例子。他们向一组患有梦游症的患者教授了一系列舞蹈动作，在梦游症中，睡眠者会进行通常在睡眠期间不会发生的身体运动。然后他们在受试者睡觉时对其进行录像。录像带上的一位女病人躺在床上，闭着眼睛，表演着她之前学过的舞蹈动作。

paragraphs.sourceText: This shows that while our bodies are at rest, our brains are drawing what's important from the information and events we've recently encountered, then integrating that data into the vast store of what
paragraphs.translationZh: 这表明，当我们的身体处于休息状态时，我们的大脑正在从我们最近遇到的信息和事件中提取重要的信息，然后将这些数据集成到海量的存储中

paragraphs.sourceText: we already know. In a 2010 study, researchers at Harvard Medical School reported that college students who dreamed about a computer maze (迷宫) task they had learned showed a 10-fold improvement in their ability to find their way through the maze compared with participants who did not dream about the task.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们已经知道了。在 2010 年的一项研究中，哈佛医学院的研究人员报告说，与没有梦想过该任务的参与者相比，梦想过所学的计算机迷宫任务的大学生在迷宫中找到出路的能力提高了 10 倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: Robert Stickgold, one of the Harvard researchers, suggests that studying right before bedtime or taking a nap following a study session in the afternoon might increase the odds of dreaming about the material. Think about that as your head hits the pillow tonight.
paragraphs.translationZh: 哈佛大学的研究人员之一罗伯特·斯蒂克戈尔德（Robert Stickgold）建议，睡前学习或下午学习结束后小睡可能会增加梦到这些材料的几率。今晚当你的头碰到枕头时想一想。
